digital-image-processing--convolution.title: convolution at one pixel
lines: g = sum(h[m][n] * f[x - m][y - n] for m in range(3) for n in range(3))
digital-image-processing--convolution.note: The output is the 3x3 neighbourhood mean, 130/9; reading f[x - m][y - n] is the kernel flip that separates convolution from correlation.

digital-image-processing--spatial-filter.title: 3x3 filter kernels
digital-image-processing--spatial-filter.note: A blur kernel's weights sum to one and preserve brightness; a derivative kernel's weights sum to zero and keep only local differences.

digital-image-processing--histogram-equa.title: histogram equalization
digital-image-processing--histogram-equa.note: The transform's slope is proportional to the input density, so the output density is flat and crowded levels are spread across the range.

digital-image-processing--wiener-filter.title: Wiener filter from MMSE
symbols: power spectrum of the true image
noise power spectrum, uncorrelated with F
digital-image-processing--wiener-filter.note: The gain is the inverse filter H*/|H|^2 tapered by S_f/S_n, so frequencies where noise dominates are attenuated instead of amplified.

digital-image-processing--huffman-coding.title: Huffman merge
lines: heap = [(wt, i, {s: ""}) for i, (s, wt) in enumerate(p.items())]
codes = {s: "0" + c for s, c in c1.items()}
codes.update({s: "1" + c for s, c in c2.items()})
digital-image-processing--huffman-coding.note: Merging the two lowest weights and prefixing the left branch with 0 and the right with 1 yields a prefix code with minimum mean length.

digital-image-processing--opening.title: morphological operators
digital-image-processing--opening.note: Opening erodes first and dilates back, so structures that vanish in the erosion never return; closing does the reverse and keeps gaps filled.

digital-image-processing--jpeg.title: JPEG encode order
digital-image-processing--jpeg.note: Quantisation is the only lossy step; the zig-zag scan and Huffman code that follow only reorder and pack what survives.

digital-image-processing--block-truncati.title: block truncation levels
symbols: pixels at or below the mean
digital-image-processing--block-truncati.note: Matching the block mean and variance with two levels gives a and b; each block then costs two levels plus a p+q bit map.
